The initiative aims to overcome the dual challenge of the scarcity of skilled manpower in jobs and the low skill level of those who are presently employed. The scheme focuses on strategically planned skill initiatives to create a skilled and certified workforce that not only contributes towards the growth of India but also drives the country into becoming the global skills capital. It encourages institutions to make the best use of the available higher education infrastructure during off-hours for skill training. This is achieved by realigning the existing infrastructure, training aids, syllabi, and curricula as per National Skills Qualifications Framework aligned qualifications. The scheme is applicable to candidates who have passed at least the tenth standard or completed ITI courses. The All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) is initiating the Kaushal Augmentation and Restructuring Mission of AICTE (KARMA) for all AICTE-approved institutions in the country. The initiative aims to overcome the dual challenge of the scarcity of skilled manpower in jobs and the low skill level of those who are presently employed. The scheme focuses on strategically planned skill initiatives to create a skilled and certified workforce that not only contributes towards the growth of India but also drives the country into becoming the global skills capital. It encourages institutions to make the best use of the available higher education infrastructure during off-hours for skill training. This is achieved by realigning the existing infrastructure, training aids, syllabi, and curricula as per National Skills Qualifications Framework aligned qualifications. The scheme is applicable to candidates who have passed at least the tenth standard or completed ITI courses. The training provided under the scheme focuses on domain-specific, demand-led skill training activities, preferably in core engineering sectors, leading directly to employment. AICTE KARMA Skill Portal: ### Document: AICTE KARMA Skill Portal | Section: Kaushal Augmentation and Restructuring Mission of AICTE (KARMA) — 2. Skilling Models

The AICTE has proposed three models for the skilling of in-school students, school dropouts, and students pursuing technical education. Model 1 targets school dropouts after they have passed class ten, including both recent and long-term dropouts. Model 2 targets advanced-level skilling for students already studying in AICTE-approved technical institutions. It introduces a skill up-gradation program for present technical students to make them industry-ready by offering advanced skilling courses during their fourth to seventh semesters, with assessments similar to the standard KARMA criteria. Model 3 integrates school education with higher education to skill students, acknowledging that education needs to shift from being corrective to connective and from transactional to relational. To establish this connection, AICTE suggests that higher education institutions start offering skill-based training for nearby school students once a week using a hub-and-spoke model. Under Model 2, **MSAJCEA** was approved to conduct five courses. India boasts one of the largest and most diverse education systems globally, with significant advancements in recent years. The introduction of new and emerging programs, increased autonomy, and widespread expansion have collectively improved access to higher education. However, these developments have also raised concerns regarding the quality and relevance of higher education. In response to these concerns, the National Policy on Education (NPE) was introduced in 1986, followed by the Programme of Action (PoA) in 1992, which outlined strategic plans for addressing these issues and advocated for the establishment of an independent national accreditation agency.

Consequently, the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) was established in 1994 as an autonomous institution under the University Grants Commission (UGC), with its headquarters located in Bengaluru. The NAAC's vision statement reflects its core mandate, which is to integrate quality assurance into the functioning of Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), thereby ensuring a commitment to excellence in education.

The National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) operates through two key bodies: the General Council (GC) and the Executive Committee (EC), both of which comprise a diverse group of educational administrators, policymakers, and senior academicians from various segments of the Indian higher education system.

At the helm of the NAAC's General Council is the Chairperson of the University Grants Commission (UGC), who serves as the President of the GC. The Chairperson of the Executive Committee, on the other hand, is an esteemed academician nominated by the President of the GC. This nomination process ensures that the EC is led by a highly respected and knowledgeable individual in the field of education.

The Director of the NAAC plays a pivotal role in the organization, serving as both the academic and administrative head. In addition to these responsibilities, the Director is also the member secretary of both the General Council and the Executive Committee, facilitating the smooth functioning of these bodies.

The Alumni Association of Mohamed Sathak A.J. College of Engineering and Architecture extends a warm welcome to all its members, inviting them to join in and reconnect with their alma mater. The primary objective of this association is to foster a strong intellectual and emotional bond between the alumni and **MSAJCEA**, thereby promoting a sense of connectedness and community.

Through the association, alumni can re-establish and renew relationships with their fellow students, as well as participate in various college activities. Moreover, the association aims to provide support to future engineers by offering assistance to those in need, in the form of funds and scholarships. It also seeks to maintain a comprehensive database of employment opportunities, facilitating placements for its members.

In addition to these initiatives, the association plans to arrange teaching and training classes for students, further contributing to the overall growth and development of **MSAJCEA**. By doing so, the Alumni Association of Mohamed Sathak A.J. College of Engineering and Architecture strives to create a positive and lasting impact on **MSAJCEA** community.
